verdict.headline: This agreement has severe liability imbalances, a tiny vendor liability cap, and a distant foreign governing law.
summary: Your liability is completely uncapped while the vendor caps their liability to just one month of fees.
The agreement auto-renews unless you give an unusually long 90-day cancellation notice.
Any legal dispute must be resolved under Delaware law rather than local Malaysian or Singaporean law.

findings.title: Uncapped customer liability versus tiny vendor cap
findings.quote: 5.1 The Customer shall be liable without limit for any loss suffered by the Vendor.
findings.why_risky: You face unlimited financial exposure for any claim, while the vendor risks almost nothing if they fail or breach the contract.
findings.standard: Liability should be mutual and capped, usually at the fees paid or payable during the previous 12 months.
findings.suggested_ask: Please make the limitation of liability mutual, set the cap at the fees paid in the previous 12 months for both parties, and apply the same exclusions and carve-outs to both.

findings.title: Vendor liability capped at only one month of fees
findings.quote: 5.2 The Vendor's total liability is limited to the fees paid in the one month before the claim.
findings.why_risky: A cap of just one month of fees means even a major outage or severe vendor failure costs them practically nothing.
findings.standard: Vendor liability should be capped at 12 months of fees.
findings.suggested_ask: Please set the vendor's liability cap to the total fees paid or payable in the preceding 12 months.

findings.title: Long 90-day auto-renewal notice requirement
findings.quote: 6.1 This Agreement renews automatically for successive 12 month terms unless the Customer gives 90 days written notice.
findings.why_risky: A 90-day notice window makes it very easy to miss the cancellation deadline and get locked into another full year.
findings.standard: Standard renewal windows require 30 days of advance notice, along with a vendor reminder before the deadline.
findings.suggested_ask: Please change renewal to 12-month periods with 30 days' notice to stop renewal, and have the vendor send a written reminder 60 days before the renewal date.

findings.title: Distant foreign governing law
findings.quote: 9.1 This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware.
findings.why_risky: Neither party operates in Delaware; defending or bringing claims under US state law would require costly foreign lawyers and travel.
findings.standard: Agreements between Malaysian and Singaporean companies should use Malaysian or Singapore law.
findings.suggested_ask: Please make the agreement subject to Malaysian law (or Singapore law) and the courts of Kuala Lumpur (or Singapore), where both parties operate.

missing_clauses.title: Personal Data Protection Clause
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: A cloud bookkeeping service processes sensitive company and personal data, so data protection rules and breach notification duties under PDPA are essential.
missing_clauses.suggested_ask: Please add a data protection clause: processing only on our instructions, reasonable security, breach notice within 48 hours, approved subcontractors, and return or deletion of data at the end.

missing_clauses.title: Confidentiality Clause
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: The contract does not bind either party to keep financial records or commercial terms confidential.
missing_clauses.suggested_ask: Please make the confidentiality obligations mutual, with the standard exceptions, lasting at least three years after the agreement ends, and require our consent before naming us publicly.

missing_clauses.title: Termination for Cause and Exit Assistance
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no mechanism for you to terminate for uncured breach or retrieve your bookkeeping data upon contract end.
missing_clauses.suggested_ask: Please give both parties the same notice period, allow 30 days to fix a breach, and add a 30-day window to export our data on termination.

disclaimer: This is an automated review to help you prepare. It is not legal advice.
